text:
maria: Heads up — since ~02:10 UTC we've seen a spike in preemptible evictions in us-west2 spot pool A. A bunch of streaming requests hit a token-stream cutover path and ~5% of those ended up 504ing instead of requeueing.

aj: Do we have the requeue header preserved across the cutover? iirc the stream-cutover proxy needs to copy X-Continue-Token -> X-Requeue-Token before swapping.

maria: Checked that — proxy emits the header but the runtime logs show 'missing requeue-key' for some requests. Logs attached below.

kevin: Can you paste the log snippet? also which deploy of cutover-proxy?

maria:
```
[02:12:05] proxy: incoming stream id=abcd conn=232, header: X-Continue-Token=tok_abc
[02:12:05] proxy: cutover initiate -> persisting kv-prefix abcd
[02:12:06] runtime: requeue lookup failed for key=tok_abc, err=not_found
[02:12:07] runtime: request timed out -> 504 -> metrics.eviction_failures++
```

kevin: Hmm looks like the token persisted but the runtime's requeue index didn't see it. Could be a race where KV write hasn't propagated to the node serving the requeue lookup. Which KV backend? memcached or redis?

sophia: It's the clustered redis with async replication (r/w node in us-west2). We recently changed max-lease-time to 30s in that pool.

aj: That could be it — async replication means the target runtime might query a follower that hasn't received the key. Two mitigation ideas: (1) make the proxy write to the requeue index in the same primary node as runtime queries (leader affinity), (2) switch to sync write for critical requeue keys during cutover.

maria: For immediate mitigation, can we extend the grace window so the proxy holds requests in-place for an extra 5s before swapping? That would reduce races.

kevin: We have grace_window_ms per node. Current is 200ms for cutovers. Bumping to 2s should help, low risk. Will that blow memory? depending on in-flight backlog.

sophia: On cost — holding big windows increases latency tail and memory usage, but cheaper than converting whole pool to on-demand. For now 2s seems fine as a temp fix.

oncall: infra-bot reports: deploy cutover-proxy v3.4.1 -> us-west2 started at 02:30 UTC :rocket: (canary 10%).

maria: Ok let's do a canary config change first: grace_window_ms=2000, requeue_write_mode=sync for requeue keys-only. Roll 10% canary then 50% if green.

aj: Also add a defensive fallback: if requeue lookup fails, attempt local in-memory prefix-check for last-known token for up to 500ms before giving 504. That reduces cold-miss surface.

kevin: Quick patch suggestion (pseudo):
```
if requeue_lookup(key) == NOT_FOUND {
  if local_cache.maybe_recent(key_prefix) { sleep(50ms); retry(); }
}
```

sophia: We should add observability: emit metric requeue_miss_race and sample failing tokens to s3 for 24h (anonymized) so we can correlate with replication lag.

maria: I'll open a tiny runbook entry: /runbooks/spot-eviction-cutover.md and note steps. Will also include rollback for grace window change.

oncall: infra-bot: runbook created at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spot-eviction-cutover.md

aj: Long term we should consider two architectural changes: (A) co-locate requeue index with proxy (write-through), (B) use a write-ahead-store that the runtime can read from local disk during cutover (fast local lookups). Both increase complexity but avoid cross-region KV races.

kevin: Agreed. For (B) maybe a compact append-only index keyed by token prefix, pruned by TTL. Could be used only during cutovers.

sophia: Add cost note — AOF will increase IO but could be limited to preemptible pools where this matters. We'll model cost impact.

maria: Action list:
- maria: roll canary with grace_window_ms=2000 + requeue_write_mode=sync (02:45 UTC)
- aj: prototype local-cache fallback + add requeue_miss_race metric (PR today)
- kevin: add sampled tokens logging to s3 (anonymize)
- sophia: run simple cost model for AOF option (EOD)

aj: also tagging this incident in #incidents with brief blurb for postmortem if canary shows >1% regression.

maria: thanks all — will update thread after canary. :thumbsup:

oncall: infra-bot: canary complete at 02:53 UTC — 10% -> metrics show requeue_miss_race dropped from 4.7% -> 0.6% in canary nodes. No latency regressions seen.

maria: Nice. Proceeding 10% -> 50% rollout now.

kevin: Note: after 50% rollout, schedule a follow-up to prototype write-ahead store in a small perf bucket.

sophia: Filing long-term design doc after this stabilizes.

maria: Closing for now, will post postmortem if any regressions appear.
